newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA says pulp outlook still uncertain.
newsitem.headline: SCA says pulp outlook still uncertain.

text.p: Swedish forest products group SCA said on Wednesday that price developments for pulp and recycled paper remain uncertain.
SCA said price recovery is slow and no positive effect on SCA's results is expected to show through until the first half of 1997 at the earliest.

SCA, announcing a 41 percent fall in profit after financial items for the first nine months of 1996 to 2.54 billion crowns ($387.2 million) , said its profits suffered from the forestry industry's cyclical downturn.
"The cycle remained weak in the third quarter and average prices for several products fell further," SCA said.
The company said announced price increases for several products, including pulp, were having a limited effect on results.
Currency fluctations hit profits by 420 million crowns.

SCA said demand was for the moment good for hygiene products and packaging products, as well as fine paper and sawn timber. "However the situation is much more uncertain for newsprint and magazine paper," the company added.
